tools.name: submit_request
tools.description: Files a feature request or data request on the user's behalf with the PokerData team. kind "data" is missing coverage (a game, format, stack depth, spot, or solve); kind "feature" is a missing capability (a tool, filter, export, or endpoint). tools.name: list_games
tools.description: Lists the covered preflop games with their stack depths and positions. "nl" = no-limit hold'em 6-max cash (169-grid hands, per-hand EV in small blinds), "nl9" = no-limit hold'em 9-max cash, "nlmtt8" = no-limit hold'em 8-max MTT chip-EV (10–300bb, 1bb BB-ante; Fold/Call/Limp/AI/Open/3B tokens), "nlh8-hydra" = no-limit hold'em 8-max MTT chip-EV with a classic 0.1bb ante from every seat (10, 20, 30, 60bb; same tokens as nlmtt8), "nlh8-icm" = no-limit hold'em 8-max MTT with ICM: one stack table per scenario (near the money, 33 or 35 left of 200, 30 paid; final table, 8 left), uneven stacks, 0.125bb ante from every seat, EVs in tournament dollars; pass scenario (the games catalog lists them; stack alone works only where one table has that depth); decision nodes only, "nlhu" = no-limit hold'em heads-up for the title, chip-EV, both players at the stack (1–40bb), 0.125bb ante each, SB on the button; decision nodes only, "plo" = pot-limit Omaha 6-max cash (4-card), "plo5" = pot-limit Omaha 5-card 6-max (100bb, 1.2bb ante), "plo9" = pot-limit Omaha 9-max cash, "plo4hu" = pot-limit Omaha 4-card heads-up cash (SB vs BB at 10bb, 20bb, 30bb, 40bb, 50bb, 75bb, 100bb or 200bb, limps allowed, 4.5% rake capped at 0.045bb; history starts "SB"), "plo6hu" = 6-card Omaha heads-up (BTN vs BB, 100bb). tools.name: list_postflop_packs
tools.description: Every solved postflop pack: preflop line, positions (OOP vs IP), stack, pot, the bet-size trees it is solved under, and the solved boards. Boards use the spaced form ("3h 3d 2s"). NLHE packs list `sizingTrees`: "75" (75% pot every street, the pack id itself) and "33" (33% pot on the flop, then 75%, under the `<pack>-flop33` id); every postflop tool accepts either tree's packId. PLO5 packs (ids starting plo5-) solve one 33% flop tree, flop decisions only. Compact output lists board names per pack. Pass `pack` (the 75% id or the -flop33 id) for that tree's per-board detail and per-flop exploitability where the index publishes a number. Missing exploitability is omitted, never estimated. Pass `variant` to list only NLHE or PLO5 packs. The returned pack ids and boards are the valid inputs for the postflop tools.

pack.description: One pack id (75% id or the -flop33 id): per-board detail and that tree's exploitability

tools.name: get_hu_plo_flop
tools.description: Heads-up PLO4 (pot-limit Omaha, four cards) flop strategy from the blueprint, at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100 or 200bb, for any of the 22,100 flops (any suits or card order). Returns the acting player's range-wide action mix and EV, how the other player's range answers each action, and, with `hand`, that four-card hand's action mix, EV and percentile in the range. BB acts first on the flop. Walk deeper by passing a returned nextLines value as `line`. Flop only: turn and river are not in the blueprint. Preflop heads-up PLO4 is the "plo4hu" preflop game.

tools.name: analyze_hu_plo_hand
tools.description: One heads-up PLO4 hand, as played, against the flop blueprint in one call: every flop decision mapped onto the blueprint tree (sizes to the nearest blueprint size), and for each of the hero's decisions the best action, every action's EV for the exact hand, the loss of the action played (bb and % of pot), whether it counts as a mistake, the hand's percentile in its range and the opponent's response to each action. Pass `hand` exactly as pokerstudy.ai's get_hand returns it in `raw.hand` (players with startingStack and cards; actions with street, actionType and amount, raises as "raise to") and `hero` (raw.hero). The stack is matched to the nearest blueprint depth. When this exact turn spot has been solved, `turnDecisions` gives the same answers for every turn decision; otherwise pass solve_turn: true to queue a GPU solve of it (about 2 to 4 minutes) and call again. Rivers work the same way: when the turn is solved and the hand reached the river, `riverDecisions` gives every river decision from an exact river solve that starts from the turn solve's own river ranges, and solve_turn: true queues that solve when it is missing.

hand.description: Parsed hand: { bigBlind, players: [{ playerName, startingStack, cards }], actions: [{ playerName, actionType, amount, street }], communityCards }.

hero.description: Hero's player name in the hand.

mistake_bb.description: Loss in bb above which a decision counts as a mistake (default 0.1).

solve_turn.description: When the hand's turn (or, once the turn is solved, river) spot is not solved yet, queue a solve for it (about 2 to 4 minutes; call again for the decisions).
